title: SHA-3 / SHAKE hash engine (FIPS 202): SHA3-224, SHA3-256, SHA3-384, SHA3-512, SHAKE128 and SHAKE256 on one Keccak-f[1600] core at one round per clock, 64-bit message and digest streams

fields.desc: 0 SHA3-224, 1 SHA3-256, 2 SHA3-384, 3 SHA3-512, 4 SHAKE128, 5 SHAKE256 (6 and 7 are refused with ERR and wipe the state)
clear the state and open a message in CTRL.mode (abandons a running message or output stream)

regs.name: MSG
regs.desc: Message word: MSG0 = bytes 3..0, MSG1 = bytes 7..4 (little-endian), then MSG2 = {last, bytes}, which commits it

fdesc.in_bytes: valid bytes, 8 except in the last word (0..8)

regs.name: DIGEST
regs.desc: Digest / SHAKE output word: DIGEST0 = bytes 3..0, DIGEST1 = bytes 7..4, DIGEST2 = last flag; reading DIGEST2 pops it

fdesc.out_last: last word of a SHA3 digest (never set for SHAKE)

fields.desc: a message or an output stream is open

irqs.name: DONE
irqs.desc: the last digest word was read

irqs.name: ERR
irqs.desc: a message word was refused (short without last, or more than 8 bytes) or start had a reserved mode

features: All six FIPS 202 functions on one Keccak-f[1600] permutation at one round per clock (24 clocks a block).
64-bit lane-wide message and digest streams with valid / ready; one clock per message word, so a rate block of SHA3-256 (17 words) takes 17 + 24 clocks: about 3.3 bytes per clock.
Messages of any length in bytes: the last word carries 0..8 valid bytes; padding (domain bits and pad10*1) is done in hardware, including the case where it needs a block of its own.
SHAKE128 / SHAKE256 give an endless output stream (any output length), permuting again after every rate block.
The 1600-bit state is cleared after a digest has been read, on every start and on reset; a start with a reserved mode wipes a SHAKE state without opening a message.
notes: SHA3-224 gives four DIGEST words; the upper 32 bits of the fourth are zero.

cSHAKE, KMAC and TupleHash (SP 800-185) are SHAKE with an encoded prefix: the host can build them by streaming the encoded strings first (cSHAKE also changes the domain bits, which this core does not offer).
Not implemented: more than one round per clock; masking against power analysis.
sequence: For each message word: wait for FLAGS.MSG_FULL = 0, write MSG0, MSG1, then MSG2 = bytes | last << 4 (bytes = 8 except in the last word; an empty message is one word with bytes 0 and last).

Read the output: wait for FLAGS.DIGEST_AVAIL, read DIGEST0, DIGEST1, DIGEST2 (DIGEST2 pops the word); for SHA3, IRQ_STATUS.DONE follows the word with last set. For SHAKE read as many words as needed, then start the next message (or CMD.start with a reserved mode to wipe the state).
verification: Core: tb/SHA3_tb.sv runs 214 cases from scripts/sha3/gen_vec.py (Python hashlib: every message length class around the rate of each function, both encodings of a message that fills its last word, SHAKE streams over several blocks) three times with different input gaps and output back-pressure, junk above the valid bytes, refused words in the middle of a message, start in every state, reserved modes and resets in the middle of a hash.

The core checker has its own Keccak-f[1600] built from FIPS 202 (round constants from the rc(t) LFSR, rho offsets from the (x, y) walk) and predicts every output word, the ready / valid timing, busy, done and err on every clock, and that the state is clear whenever the core is idle.
